context: A 60-node force-directed social network where node radius encodes 'influence' (right-skewed synthetic data) and color encodes sentiment via a diverging scale; users can toggle between sqrt, linear, and log radius mappings to observe perceptual distortion.
first_impression: Intentionally educational about encoding honesty, with sqrt as the correct default and linear/log offered as deliberate distortion examples.
what_works: Default uses d3.scaleSqrt mapping influence to radius, making area linearly proportional to data (correct); domain is data-driven via d3.extent(nodes, d => d.influence), and node joins use a key function d => d.id ensuring object constancy on scale transitions.
what_doesnt: Size legend uses hardcoded sample values [10, 30, 60, 100] rather than data-driven quantiles, so it may misrepresent the actual distribution; the sqrt range [rMin=4, rMax=32] is fixed regardless of data spread, meaning the visual area ratio (64x) can diverge from the actual influence ratio under different datasets.
